title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
A foreign government funded the creation of a fake American think tank designed to influence how AI systems respond to questions about contested geopolitical topics. The Hanover Institute published over 560,000 words of content formatted to look like neutral academic research while advocating specific government positions. The operation demonstrates a deployment failure: AI systems trained on web data ingested material designed to manipulate them, without mechanisms to identify fabricated sources or distinguish advocacy from scholarship.

The infrastructure built for this operation targeted a specific vulnerability in how large language models acquire training data. The operatives used a platform optimized for chatbot citations, meaning they engineered the content explicitly to appear in AI system outputs. It is not established whether this campaign succeeded in changing any AI system's responses, or how many commercial models ingested the material.

The failure required multiple breakdowns in the pipeline from content creation to model training. No verification checked whether the think tank's purported identity matched its legal status or staffing. No filter examined whether academic-looking content from unknown organizations should carry the weight of primary sources. The poisoning of training data is preventable through source verification and detection of coordinated inauthentic publishing, but it is not established that any safeguard caught this campaign before it was reported by journalists.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

Israeli-funded operatives created a fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute to influence artificial intelligence systems toward pro-Israel messaging. Between August 6 and 14, 2026, the site published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words designed to appear academic and neutral while presenting Israeli government positions on topics including alleged war crimes, genocide accusations, and the Gaza blockade. The operation used a specialized platform designed to optimize content for chatbot citations, and the New York media firm Piro Inc filed the site as foreign agent material with the US Justice Department. The fake institute has no legal entity status, named staff, or physical address, though it later added a funding page acknowledging external support.

The broader campaign involved tens of millions of dollars routed through the European advertising company Havas Media to multiple American firms, including Clock Tower X run by former Trump campaign manager Brad Parscale. Israeli officials have expressed frustration that the expensive public diplomacy efforts failed to improve Israel's standing in American public opinion, which has significantly declined with 60 percent of Americans holding unfavorable views by April 2026. Researchers warn the operation demonstrates how foreign governments and other actors can now poison training data used by commercial AI models, potentially influencing chatbot responses without traceable sources.
